questions.q: How many profiles can a single user have at one time?
options: Zero
Exactly one
Up to three
Unlimited
questions.explain: Profile is the single mandatory permission container; every user has exactly one.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four categories of access a profile controls?
options: Object permissions
Field-level security
App visibility
Report folder sharing
questions.explain: Profiles control object permissions, field-level security, app visibility, and system permissions — not report folder sharing specifically.

questions.q: Can a standard profile like Standard User be edited directly?
options: Yes, directly from the profile list
No — standard profiles can be viewed but not edited; you clone them instead
Only System Administrators can edit standard profiles
Only in Salesforce Classic, not Lightning
questions.explain: Standard profiles are locked by Salesforce. To get an editable version, you clone it into a new custom profile.

questions.q: What does cloning a profile actually do?
options: Deletes the original profile
Creates a new, fully editable profile starting from the original's settings
Merges two existing profiles into one
Converts a profile into a permission set
questions.explain: Clone Profile copies an existing profile's settings into a new, editable profile under a new name.

questions.q: How do permission sets and permission set groups relate to a user's profile?
options: They replace the profile entirely
They only ever add access on top of the profile, never remove it
They can only be assigned instead of a profile, not alongside one
They override and can revoke profile-granted permissions
questions.explain: A user's profile sets the baseline; permission sets and permission set groups only add to that baseline, as covered in the next two lessons.
